title: Ivo and the Hollow
premise: When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Marguerite Ishikawa discovers that the outlawed magic he was taught as a child is the only thing keeping a hungry entity called the Hollow from devouring the world. The wards were fed for centuries by a bloodline of wardens — and Marguerite is its last heir, his master having hidden him to spare him that fate. Hunted by the Crown's witch-finders, courted by a rebel cabal who want to weaponize the Hollow, and shadowed by Ivo, a warden-ghost bound to his blood who is not what he seems, Marguerite must choose between sealing the Hollow forever at the cost of all magic and memory, or feeding it himself. In the end he refuses both options: he binds the Hollow into his own name, becoming the living ward — mortal, remembered by no one but Ivo, who chooses to forget everything except him.
about_author: Kestrel Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog, they insist, is doing something on purpose.

chapters.title: Charms for a Starless City
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He sells a luck-knot to a dockworker in Ashfall City, hiding his craft from the Wardens' patrols, and pays his rent with money he shouldn't have. When the city bells begin tolling wrong — thirteen times — and every star overhead gutters out, his protective charms burn black in their pouches. Beat: dread arriving quietly, the ordinary world cracking.

chapters.title: The Night the Wards Fell
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Riots spread as the border wards fail; refugees pour in carrying stories of a darkness that eats names. A dying woman presses an iron signet ring into his hand and says 'the Hollow knows your face.' His old master's warning — never let them find you — finally makes sense. Beat: inheritance as curse, the past demanding payment.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fleeing through the flooded undercity, he is cornered by witch-finders and saved by a stranger who steps out of a wall: Ivo, translucent, bound to the signet ring, claiming to be the ghost of the last warden. Ivo calls him 'heir' and refuses to explain further. Beat: uneasy alliance; the first hint that Ivo is lying about something.

chapters.title: What the Master Buried
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to age eleven. He returns to his abandoned apprenticeship cottage and finds his master's hidden journal: the Ishikawa line has fed the border wards with their own lives for four hundred years, and Marguerite was smuggled away to break the chain. Beat: grief and fury — his whole runaway life was someone else's decision.

chapters.title: The Witch-Finders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Captain Serane Voss's POV. Voss, head of the Crown's witch-finders, reads a report that the fallen wards were warden-made and that a surviving Ishikawa may live in Ashfall. She is pragmatic, not cruel, and believes restoring the wards is the only way to save the city. Beat: antagonist with a point; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: The Cabal of the Open Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A rebel cell called the Open Door finds him first, led by the charismatic Odile Ferrant, who argues the wards were slavery and the Hollow should be bargained with, not starved. She offers protection, purpose, and a family. Marguerite, raw from the journal, almost says yes. Beat: temptation of belonging over truth.

chapters.title: Lessons in Dead Magic
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV (first time). Ivo teaches Marguerite the warden craft — how to hear the Hollow moving beneath the land like water under ice — while concealing that each lesson burns away more of Ivo's own substance. He remembers a promise made to Marguerite's grandmother. Beat: tenderness built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ivo travel toward the old warden seat and pass a village the Hollow has already touched: everyone alive, smiling, and unable to recall their own children's faces. Marguerite realizes the Hollow doesn't kill — it erases, and the Crown's 'peace' since the wards fell is already a kind of forgetting. Beat: horror of the stakes made intimate.

chapters.title: Serane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss catches up to them and offers Marguerite clemency in exchange for rekindling the wards under Crown control — meaning a life spent as a state furnace. Ivo urges refusal; Voss points out the rebels will simply use him worse. Marguerite escapes rather than choose. Beat: every door leads to a cage.

chapters.title: Blood and Iron
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the ruined warden seat, Marguerite attempts the rite alone and fails catastrophically, tearing open a wound in the world that lets the Hollow taste his name. Ivo saves him by spending half of what remains of himself. Beat: hubris punished; the cost of going it alone.

chapters.title: What Ivo Is
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Truth surfaces: Ivo is not a dead warden but a fragment of the Hollow itself, cut loose generations ago and bound to the ring as a jailer — and a spy, however unwilling. Every lesson taught Marguerite also taught the Hollow. Beat: betrayal, and the question of whether a thing made to betray can choose otherwise.

chapters.title: The Door in the Dark
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Devastated, Marguerite walks into the Hollow's borderland deliberately, seeking answers at the source. There he meets the entity wearing his master's voice, offering restoration of everything erased — his childhood, his master, even Ivo made whole — if he opens the way willingly. Beat: the seduction of grief.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite rejects the bargain, understanding at last that the Hollow feeds on longing for what's lost, and that accepting the offer would erase the very grief that makes him himself. He escapes wounded but clear-eyed, carrying knowledge of the Hollow's true hunger. Beat: the theme crystallized — survival that costs your self isn't survival.

chapters.title: Ashfall Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The Hollow, denied Marguerite, turns on Ashfall; the Cabal seizes the chaos to force open the old warden gate; Voss must choose between her orders and the city. Marguerite arrives to find the people who bought his charms standing in the streets, holding them like talismans. Beat: convergence; small kindnesses mattering.

chapters.title: Odile's Faith
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Inside the seized gatehouse, Odile reveals she lost her family to the old wards' tithe and genuinely believes opening the Door frees everyone from inherited sacrifice. Her plan requires an Ishikawa's consent — forged if necessary. Beat: antagonist as mirror; righteous conviction curdling into coercion.

chapters.title: The Conscription of Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captured by the Cabal, Marguerite is told the rite can be performed with his blood whether he consents or not. Ivo, presumed gone after his exposure, appears within the Cabal's ranks — having offered himself to them to reach Marguerite. Beat: lowest point; trust broken and inexplicably offered again.

chapters.title: A Third Answer
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ivo's alternating POV. In a cell, they build the forbidden option neither side wants: not sealing the Hollow away nor feeding it, but binding it into a living name — a person who carries the ward inside themselves, mortal and free, needing no bloodline, no prison, no lie. It will erase the bearer from every memory but one. Beat: hope engineered from ruin.

chapters.title: The Gatehouse Rite
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. As the Cabal begins the forced rite and the Hollow pours through the gate, Marguerite hijacks the working mid-cast, using their circle, his blood, and Ivo's anchor-spell together. Voss, choosing the city over her orders, holds the Cabal off with her witch-finders. Beat: climax begins; enemies becoming allies under pressure.

chapters.title: Ivo's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The binding needs a fragment of the Hollow willing to serve as its keystone — Ivo himself. He accepts, dissolving into the new ward woven through Marguerite's name, and spends his final moments making Marguerite promise not to remember him gently but truly. Beat: sacrifice reframed as agency; love without possession.

chapters.title: The Hollow Made Human
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The Hollow collapses inward, sealed inside Marguerite, who survives — changed, marked with warden-sigils along his arms, able to feel the world's edges but no longer able to work magic outward. Odile, broken by the failure of her faith, surrenders; Voss covers the truth publicly as a 'ward restoration.' Beat: victory that costs identity.

chapters.title: The Forgetting
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The binding takes its price: memories of Ivo dissolve day by day, like the village that forgot its children. Marguerite writes everything down, then chooses to burn the pages — because a ward carried in resentment would crack, and Ivo asked to be remembered truly or not at all. Beat: grief accepted as the shape of love.

chapters.title: Stars, Again
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue. A year later, stars have returned over Ashfall; magic remains outlawed but tolerated in small charms, and Marguerite sells them still, feeling the Hollow sleep warm beneath his ribs. One evening a translucent stranger hesitates at his stall, drawn by something he cannot name, and Marguerite — remembering nothing, knowing everything — offers him tea. Beat: quiet resurrection; the story ends where love began.
